abstract.p: The invention relates to a binding assembly (605) for use with a digital printer (706), having a support frame for mounting a printhead assembly and for printing on pages of media (604) passing into the binding assembly including: binding means for applying a binding material to the pages of the media along a line substantially parallel to a general direction of travel of the media with respect with the support frame.

L'invention concerne un ensemble de reliure (605) qui s'utilise avec une imprimante numérique (706). L'ensemble de reliure comprend un cadre-support pour monter un ensemble tête d'impression et pour imprimer sur des pages d'un support (604) défilant à l'intérieur de l'ensemble de reliure. Il comprend en outre un moyen de reliure pour appliquer un matériau de reliure sur les pages du support, le long d'une ligne sensiblement parallèle à une direction générale de la course du support par rapport au cadre-support.

description.p: PRINTED MEDIA PARALLEL BINDER
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to printed media production and in particular binding pages of printed media into bound documents
CO-PENDING APPLICATIONS

Various methods, systems and apparatus relating to the present invention are disclosed in the following co- pending applications filed by the applicant or assignee of the present invention simultaneously with the present application
The disclosures of these co-pending applications are incorporated herein by cross-reference
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

With the advent of the Internet has come the opportunity for the print media industry to publish "on-line" rather than producing and distributing traditional paper based publications On-line publishing has a number of advantages From the consumer's point of view, information is available on demand, information can be navigated via hypertext links, information can be searched, and information can be automatically personalised From the publisher's point of view, the costs of printing and physical distribution are eliminated and the publication becomes more attractive to advertisers as it can be targeted to specific demographics and linked to product sites On-line publication also has disadvantages Computer screens are inferior to paper At the same quality as a magazine page, a SVGA computer screen displays only about a fifth as much information Both CRT's (Cathode Ray Tubes) and LCD's (Liquid Crystal Displays) have brightness and contrast problems, particularly, when ambient light is strong Ink on paper, being reflective rather than emissive is both bright and sharp in ambient light Accordingly, people have a natural preference to read newspapers, magazines, catalogues, brochures and other publications in a bound paper based format
- la - Known digital printers, and in particular digital Inkjet printers, do not make any provision for binding together the pages of printed media Such an arrangement would conveniently provide for bound document production in the small office/home office (SOHO) environment This would also permit some of the existing drawbacks of on-line publication to be addressed However, for this arrangement to be widely adopted it can not be inconveniently slow Therefore, any provision for binding separate pages into a bound document must not add a significant amount of time to the production of the document
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

It is an object of the present invention to provide means to bmd pages of pπnted media into bound documents suitable for use m conjunction with a digital printer Accordingly, the present invention provides a bmdmg assembly for use with a digital printer havmg a support frame for mounting a pπnthead assembly for pπntmg on pages of media, the bmdmg assembly including bmdmg means for applymg bmdmg mateπal to the pages of the media along a lme substantially parallel to a general direction of travel of the media with respect with the support frame

Preferably, the bmdmg means mcludes a glue wheel positioned to engage one surface of a pπnted page as it exits the pπnthead assembly In a particularly preferred form the bmdmg means further mcludes a collection and compression means for aligning each page in a document to be bound and pressing the adhesive coated portion of a page against the adjacent page In a further prefeπed form the binding means does not apply adhesive to the first page of a document to be bound and then applies adhesive to the front side of each subsequent page such that the compression means engages the reverse side of each subsequent page and sequentially presses it against the previous page It will be appreciated that the bmdmg means according to this embodiment applies the adhesive directly pnor to pressmg the adhesive against the previous page This is more effective than applymg adhesive to the rear of each page and sequentially pressmg each page to the subsequent page because any interruption m the pπntmg process such as replenishing the paper supply may allow the adhesive applied to the last adhered page to deteπorate and become less effective In some embodiments of the present invention, the glue wheel is adapted to receive adhesive from an adhesive supply by capillary action It is preferable if the glue wheel is retained m a chamber that is sealed to provide an environment for substantially maintaining the adhesive performance when the glue wheel is not m use

In some embodiments, a powered cam shaft is engaged to advance the glue wheel through a closable aperture in the chamber mto engagement with the surface of the page In these embodiments, it is preferable if a flexible pad is positioned opposite the glue wheel to maintain a substantially constant pressure between the page and the glue wheel dunng the application of adhesive

In some forms of the invention the pπnthead is adapted to print the full width of the page simultaneously It will be appreciated that by providing a bmdmg assembly that binds the pages along a line parallel to the direction of travel of the page, the binding process can at least be initiated while the printer is pπntmg the page thereby reducing the time required for document production The present invention also allows the production of pπnted mateπal m the traditionally appealing form of a bound document rather than separate pages With the aid of modern printers and computer network technology, the invention has many applications in on-line publication of newspapers, magazines, brochures and so on The present mvention will be descπbed with particular reference to the netpage system An overview of this system is set out below It has been developed to allow a large number of distπbuted users to mteract with networked information via prmted matter and optical sensors thereby to obtain interactive pπnted matter on demand from high-speed networked color printers

In the preferred embodiment, the invention is configured to work with the netpage system, an overview of which follows The system is descπbed in this specification to reduce the need for external reference when attempting to understand the context in which the preferred embodiments and aspects of the present mvention operate In its preferred form, the netpage system relies on the production of, and human interaction with, netpages These are pages of text, graphics and images pπnted on ordinary paper, but which work like interactive

Web pages Information is encoded on each page usmg ink, which is substantially mvisible to the unaided human eye The ink, however, and thereby the encoded information, can be sensed by an optically imagmg pen (the netpage pen) and transmitted to the netpage system

In the prefeπed form, active buttons and hyperlinks on each page can be clicked with the netpage pen to request information from the network or to signal preferences to a network server In one embodiment, text wπtten by hand on a netpage is automatically recognized via the pen, allowing forms to be filled m In other embodiments, signatures recorded on a netpage are automatically venfied, allowing e-commerce transactions to be securely authonzed

The netpage pen works in conjunction with a netpage printer, an Internet-connected pπntmg appliance for home, office or mobile use The pen is wireless and communicates securely with the netpage pnnter via a short-range radio link The netpage pnnter delivers, peπodically or on demand, personalized newspapers, magazmes, catalogs, brochures and other publications, all pnnted at high quality as mteractive netpages Unlike a personal computer, the netpage pnnter is an appliance which can be, for example, wall-mounted adjacent an area where the morning news is

A netpage pnnter pnnts pages of photographic-quality images and magazme quality text at a rate of over 30 double sided sheets per minute (that is, more than 60 pages per minute) They come m a vaπety of forms, including wall-mounted versions, tabletop versions, portable versions, and pocket versions Given the nature of the netpage system, it is envisaged that one of the most commercially relevant forms of netpage pnnter will be the wall mounted version refeπed to as wallpnnter For convemence, the present mvention will be descnbed m detail with reference to this specific version shown m the accompanying drawings

The vertically-mounted netpage wallpnnter 600 is shown fully assembled m Figures 1 and 2 As best shown m Figures 2, 2a and 19, it pnnts Netpages on A4 sized media usmg duplexed 8' _" Memjet™ pnnt engmes 602 and 603 It uses a straight paper path with the paper 604 passmg through duplexed pnnt engmes 602 and 603 which pnnt both sides of a sheet simultaneously, m full color and with full bleed A multi-DSP raster image processor (RIP) rasteπzes pages to internal memory, and a pair of custom pπnt engine controllers expand, dither and pπnt page images to the duplexed pnntheads m real time

An integral bmdmg assembly 605 applies a stπp of glue along one edge of each printed sheet, allowing it to adhere to the previous sheet when pressed agamst it This creates a final bound document 618 which can range m thickness from one sheet to several hundred sheets The bmdmg assembly will be considered m close detail below with particular reference to Figures 13, 14 and 15

Figure 4, shows the complete assembly of the replaceable ink cartndge 627 It has bladders or chambers for storing fixative 644, adhesive 630, and cyan 631 , magenta 632, yellow 633, black 634 and infrared 635 inks The cartndge 627 also contains a micro air filter 636 m a base moldmg 637 As shown m Figure 9, the micro air filter 636 mterfaces with an air pump 638 mside the pnnter via a hose 639 This provides filtered air to the pnntheads 705 to prevent ingress of micro particles into the Memjet™ pnntheads 705 which may clog the nozzles By incorporating the air filter 636 within the cartndge 627, the operational life of the filter is effectively linked to the life of the cartndge This ensures that the filter is replaced together with the cartndge rather than relymg on the user to clean or replace the filter at the required intervals Furthermore, the adhesive and infrared ink are replenished together with the visible inks and air filter thereby reducmg how frequently the pnnter operation is interrupted because of the depletion of a consumable mateπal

The cartndge 627 has a thm wall casmg 640 The ink bladders 631 to 635 and fixitive bladder 644 are suspended within the casing by a pm 645 which hooks the cartndge together The single glue bladder 630 is accommodated in the base molding 637 This is a fully recyclable product with a capacity for printing and gluing 3000 pages (1500 sheets)

The paper exits the first Memjet™ pπnt engme 602 through a set of powered exit spike wheels (aligned along the straight paper path), which acts against a rubberized roller These spike wheels contact the 'wet' prmted surface and continue to feed the sheet 604 mto the second Memjet™ pπnt engine 603

As shown m Figures 2, 2a, 9, 13 and 14, the paper 604 passes from the duplexed pπnt engmes 602 and 603, into the bmder assembly 605 The prmted page passes between a powered spike wheel axle 670 with a fibrous support roller and another movable axle with spike wheels and a momentary action glue wheel 673 The movable axle/glue assembly 673 is mounted to a metal support bracket and it is transported forward to mterface with the powered axle 670 by action of a camshaft 642 A separate motor powers 675 this camshaft Both motors 676 are controlled by the Memjet™ pnntheads The glue wheel assembly 673 consists of a partially hollow axle 679 with a rotating couplmg 680 for the glue supply hose 641 from the ink cartndge 627 This axle 679 connects to a glue wheel 681 , which absorbs adhesive by capillary action through radial holes A molded housmg surrounds the glue wheel 681 , with an opening at the front Pivoting side moldmgs 683 and sprung outer doors 684 are attached to the metal support bracket and lunge out sideways when the rest of the assembly 673 is thrust forward This action exposes the glue wheel 681 through the front of the molded housmg Tension springs 685 close the assembly and effectively cap the glue wheel 681 dunng penods of inactivity

As the sheet 604 passes mto the glue wheel assembly 673, adhesive is applied to one vertical edge on the front side (apart from the first sheet of a document) as it is transported down into the bmdmg assembly 605 It will be appreciated that this arrangement applies adhesive to each page dunng pπnting so that the paper movement through the pnnter is not interrupted or stopped at a separate gluing station This mcreases the pnnter speed, however, it requires that the pages move through the pnnter in "portrait" configuration (that is, m a direction parallel to the long edges) This in turn requues the paper tray, binding station and collection station to be m portrait configuration This mav make the overall length of the pnnter too great to convemently fit mto areas having limited space In these situations, the media tray, bmding station and collection station can be arranged in "landscape" onentation (short sides parallel to paper movement) to shorten the length of the pnnter However, the gluing assembly must still be able to apply glue along the long side of the pages In this version of wallpnnter (not shown), the adhesive is applied to the longitudinal edge of each page with a reciprocating glue stnp

The cable 693 is sprung to allow for positive pressure to be applied to the previous sheet to aid bmdmg Furthermore, the angled platen 689 is shallower at the top than at the base m order to support the document 618 m an over axis configuration

A sensor (not shown) operatively connected to the control of the stepper motor, may be used to determine the position of the last page bound to the document to allow the platen to accurately adhere the next page to it

A paper tapper 643 knocks the sheet 604 to one side of the binder 605 as it is transported across to the angled platen 689 The mam PCB 612 controls motors 695, 696 and 697 for the cable winder shaft 694, the tapper 643 and the exit hatch 690 respectively

619 Plastic foils 698 on the lower front moldmg 610 work together with the hatch 690 to direct the finished document 618 to the back of the collection tray 619 and feed any further documents mto the tray without hitting existing ones A plurality the flexible foils may be provided, each having different lengths to accommodate documents havmg different page sizes The collection tray 619 is molded in clear plastic and pulls out of its socket under a certain loading Access for removmg documents is provided on three sides
